title: Design review loop
idea: A peer review is a structured read of your design by another engineer, who questions responsibilities and change points while you explain, decide and revise.
points: Send a one-page summary first: use cases, class diagram, and the trade-offs you chose.
Good comments name a scenario: who changes this class when a rule changes?
Label each comment blocking or optional, so the author knows what must change.
Answer every comment with a change or a reason; an unanswered comment looks ignored.

hero.title: One review round on the capstone

items.label: Self-review
items.text: Re-read the diagram against the use cases. Remove what no requirement needs.

items.label: Walkthrough
items.text: Trace one `book` call aloud, from `BookingService` to each listener.

items.label: Comments
items.text: On the first draft, the reviewer asks why `BookingService` sends email itself. Tagged blocking.

items.label: Decide
items.text: You agree: email is a reaction, so it moves behind `BookingListener`.

items.label: Revise
items.text: Push the change, link it in the thread, and re-run every test.

items.label: Approve
items.text: The reviewer resolves the thread. Optional comments go to a follow-up list.

code.title: A comment and its fix
code.caption: From an early draft: one blocking design comment, answered with the smallest change that removes the concern.

takeaway: Review the design's reasons, not its formatting, and answer every comment.
